title: Workspace wall / angled view

location.series: COLLINS / Figma / Nothing Great Is Made Alone case study

slide_intent: Inspect an identity from an oblique view because depth and overlap can change how a physical application reads.
strategic_value: Raised lettering and layered stars can give Figma’s workspace identity a tactile presence beyond its screen graphics.
demonstration: An angled wall view reveals the thickness, shadows and overlapping arrangement of the campaign letters and colored motifs.
practical_value: Compare a front-facing composition with its physical depth and side-view legibility.

content_islands.name: Raised statement
content_islands.spec: Show black letters standing off the perforated wood surface.

content_islands.name: Layered motifs
content_islands.spec: Place colored stars across and beside the letters, retaining their projected edges and shadows.

content_islands.name: Near selection frame
content_islands.spec: Keep the blue outlined frame and cursor objects in the lower-right foreground.

reference_purposes.Application: The angled photograph shows the depth and layering of the environmental identity.
